ci_support_linux_64_.yaml:
channel_sources:
- conda-forge
channel_targets:
- conda-forge main
cran_mirror:
- https://cloud.r-project.org
docker_image:
- quay.io/condaforge/linux-anvil-x86_64:alma10
target_platform:
- linux-64

about.summary: Extension of 'ggplot2', 'ggstatsplot' creates graphics with details from statistical tests included in the plots themselves. It provides an easier syntax to generate information-rich plots for statistical analysis of continuous (violin plots, scatterplots, histograms, dot plots, dot-and-whisker plots) or categorical (pie and bar charts) data. Currently, it supports the most common types of statistical approaches and tests: parametric, nonparametric, robust, and Bayesian versions of t-test/ANOVA, correlation analyses, contingency table analysis, meta-analysis, and regression analyses. References: Patil (2021) <doi:10.21105/joss.03236>.

name: r-ggstatsplot
raw_meta_yaml:
{% set version = "1.1.1" %}
{% set posix = 'm2-' if win else '' %}

package:
  name: r-ggstatsplot
  version: {{ version|replace("-", "_") }}

source:
  url:
    - {{ cran_mirror }}/src/contrib/ggstatsplot_{{ version }}.tar.gz
    - {{ cran_mirror }}/src/contrib/Archive/ggstatsplot/ggstatsplot_{{ version }}.tar.gz
  sha256: fde68c505510240a5a1b416efccf4c29e4ab5bf3ee257932103ead86a3f1f5e8

build:
  number: 0
  noarch: generic
  rpaths:
    - lib/R/lib/
    - lib/
  missing_dso_whitelist:
    - '*/R.dll'        # [win]
    - '*/Rblas.dll'    # [win]
    - '*/Rlapack.dll'  # [win]

requirements:
  build:
    - {{ posix }}zip               # [win]
    - cross-r-base {{ r_base }}    # [build_platform != target_platform]
  host:
    - r-base >=4.5.0
    - r-correlation >=0.8.8
    - r-datawizard >=1.3.1
    - r-dplyr >=1.2.1
    - r-forcats >=1.0.1
    - r-ggcorrplot >=0.3.0
    - r-ggplot2 >=4.0.3
    - r-ggrepel >=0.9.8
    - r-ggside >=0.4.1
    - r-ggsignif >=0.6.4
    - r-glue >=1.8.1
    - r-insight >=1.5.2
    - r-paletteer >=1.7.0
    - r-parameters >=0.29.2
    - r-patchwork >=1.3.2
    - r-performance >=0.17.1
    - r-purrr >=1.2.2
    - r-rlang >=1.3.0
    - r-statsexpressions >=2.1.1
    - r-tidyr >=1.3.2
  run:
    - r-base >=4.5.0
    - r-correlation >=0.8.8
    - r-datawizard >=1.3.1
    - r-dplyr >=1.2.1
    - r-forcats >=1.0.1
    - r-ggcorrplot >=0.3.0
    - r-ggplot2 >=4.0.3
    - r-ggrepel >=0.9.8
    - r-ggside >=0.4.1
    - r-ggsignif >=0.6.4
    - r-glue >=1.8.1
    - r-insight >=1.5.2
    - r-paletteer >=1.7.0
    - r-parameters >=0.29.2
    - r-patchwork >=1.3.2
    - r-performance >=0.17.1
    - r-purrr >=1.2.2
    - r-rlang >=1.3.0
    - r-statsexpressions >=2.1.1
    - r-tidyr >=1.3.2

test:
  commands:
    - $R -e "library('ggstatsplot')"           # [not win]
    - "\"%R%\" -e \"library('ggstatsplot')\""  # [win]

about:
  home: https://indrajeetpatil.github.io/ggstatsplot/
  dev_url: https://github.com/IndrajeetPatil/ggstatsplot
  license: MIT
  summary: 'Extension of ''ggplot2'', ''ggstatsplot'' creates graphics with details from statistical
    tests included in the plots themselves. It provides an easier syntax to generate
    information-rich plots for statistical analysis of continuous (violin plots, scatterplots,
    histograms, dot plots, dot-and-whisker plots) or categorical (pie and bar charts)
    data. Currently, it supports the most common types of statistical approaches and
    tests: parametric, nonparametric, robust, and Bayesian versions of t-test/ANOVA,
    correlation analyses, contingency table analysis, meta-analysis, and regression
    analyses. References: Patil (2021) <doi:10.21105/joss.03236>.'
  license_family: MIT
  license_file:
    - '{{ environ["PREFIX"] }}/lib/R/share/licenses/MIT'
    - LICENSE

extra:
  recipe-maintainers:
    - conda-forge/r
